rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That flat-pack cupboard's leaning. I could take a look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold it for a second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

card.title: Admit You Need Me
card.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my jumper beside your broken heater.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not cold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll put the spare blanket away too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Leave the blanket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shall I leave myself? I know where the fuse box is.

card.title: Admit You Need Me
card.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you get your train, could you taste this soup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

card.title: Don’t Go
card.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've packed your suitcase upside down. Let me show you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A suitcase doesn't have an upside down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain these shoes facing the handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. After we settle the shoes. It's a long journey.

card.title: Don’t Go
card.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've bought a replacement mug. Not that anyone needs to say anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did I break your mug?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting that you started there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about the mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that tone. Think a little more recently.

card.title: Say You’re Sorry
card.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely day for clearing the air, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are we opening a window?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Some things require more than ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have I upset you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's an excellent opening. I'd keep going.

card.title: Say You’re Sorry
card.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you support a small improvement to the front garden?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What sort of improvement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something with a pond. And no tree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where's the tree?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

card.title: Retroactive Permission
card.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So standing guests would be more considerate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you answer before they ring again?

card.title: Retroactive Permission
card.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You do such beautiful handwriting. Even your bin labels are elegant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Imagine what you could do with these eighty place cards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you asking me to write them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wouldn't presume. I'm leaving room for your artistic impulse.

card.title: Make It Their Idea
card.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've always said this shed could be organised better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cleared Saturday so I won't interrupt your vision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want me to clean it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if that still feels like your idea.

card.title: Make It Their Idea
card.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you say you heard about the party, which part?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bit with the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before or after it reached the balcony?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened on the balcony?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing confirmed. Who's been using that word?

card.title: How Much Do You Know?
card.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What did the manager say about the missing keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That they're missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No mention of a drain, then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should there be?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking how thorough the briefing was.

card.title: How Much Do You Know?
card.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need a lookout for a surprise dinner. Can you whistle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who are we surprising?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum. She mustn't find the cake in the shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not use the kitchen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because that's your second assignment. Distract her from it.

card.title: Join Me
card.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the office at seven. Bring wrapping paper, not questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is this another secret leaving party?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need someone who can keep a straight face around balloons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who is leaving?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Join the committee and you'll get a balloon with the name.

card.title: Join Me
card.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That staff-only door might lead to the roof garden. Try it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone should stay here looking uninvolved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not allowed through either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll learn the rule together, with you slightly ahead.

card.title: You First
card.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste a grape before buying them. Quality control.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signs can't taste. You'll have better information.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taste one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to compare your reaction with the official policy.

card.title: You First
card.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole town's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who stopped it leaning into the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

card.title: Recognize Me
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've thanked the wedding guests. What about the person who cooked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make an announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.

card.title: Recognize Me
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead of the concert. I've made your favourite cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cake has your name on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can visit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow it will have my name. Choose carefully.

card.title: Choose Me
card.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take me on the expedition. I can read maps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So can the guide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the guide remember your coffee order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're crossing a desert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You'll want someone who knows you take it iced.

card.title: Choose Me
card.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before catching your train, turn the biscuit clockwise three times in thanks for the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've eaten it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the gratitude must continue through a second biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly enough for the departure dunk, provided we begin respectfully.

bespokePairs.seedUse: The Stance's tea/biscuit ritual supplies escalating reasons for delaying departure without a direct demand to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can't pack the teacup before we've performed the final household blessing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said goodbye to the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A personal goodbye. The cup still awaits its clockwise farewell.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I do that on the train?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not without the kitchen. Better unpack it while I fetch the biscuit.

bespokePairs.seedUse: The Stance's tea/biscuit ritual supplies escalating reasons for delaying departure without a direct demand to stay.

card.title: Sacred Procedure
card.instruction: Treat an ordinary activity as a solemn ritual. Protect every step, object, and tradition from casual interference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please leave your sandwich wrapped. The picnic begins with three taps on the basket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The basket's in the car. Sam's driven off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we wait. This is a picnic, not people eating near each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll phone Sam. He can tap the basket for us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on speaker. No one unwraps anything until we hear the third tap.

beats.text: We acknowledge the light before approaching the shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bulb's broken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today we open it in remembrance.

beats.text: Your note says 'regretfully.' A valid clearing of the air begins with 'sorry.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry for what?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The opening word must be correct before we discuss its object.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add my name so I know which relationship your excellent beginning applies to.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A will accept an unspoken-offence apology only with one exact formal marker; the tiny wording feature becomes A's way to manoeuvre toward remorse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we enjoy tea, could you put a full stop after your apology?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't apologised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explains why the sentence feels incomplete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What sentence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'I'm sorry' and we'll find the correct punctuation together.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A will accept an unspoken-offence apology only with one exact formal marker; the tiny wording feature becomes A's way to manoeuvre toward remorse.

card.title: The Detail That Makes It Official
card.instruction: Choose one tiny procedural detail—wording, order, timing, seating, or a mark—and treat it as the only source of legitimacy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This marriage certificate has the dot above the wrong letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've been married twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twenty years together. But until that dot moves, this doesn't certify a marriage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then move it. Our anniversary party starts at seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. But we'll need a wedding cake. This dot makes tonight our first day.

card.title: The Detail That Makes It Official

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your club resignation has the seal upside down. You're still our secretary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've moved abroad. Rotate the page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. Now your resignation is valid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. You can stop sending me the minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll rotate the previous eleven too. We may owe you a year's subscriptions.

card.title: Say You’re Sorry

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's an excellent opening. I'd keep going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've labelled all eighty wedding cards except the names. Your handwriting is so beautiful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want me to finish them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if the unfinished part inspires you more than it exhausted me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could have asked earlier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've prepared a lovely space for you to volunteer now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I sorted everyone's lunch again. You arrange sandwiches so attractively.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you giving me lunch duty?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wouldn't impose. I've merely exhausted myself beside your obvious gift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll do tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. I'll make you a checklist while resenting how long recognition took.

card.title: The Responsible One
card.instruction: Take responsibility for everyone and everything. Fix problems before anyone asks, then resent having to do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your lunch and labelled your umbrella. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working from home today. You can leave it to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put your lunch in the fridge. Apparently I need your work calendar too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll share it with you. Tomorrow says lunch out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll book you a table, then. Now I have to ring and check they have somewhere for your umbrella.

beats.text: I've cleaned the kitchen while you slept. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to clean it at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And leave me knowing it was dirty until nine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Next time, wake me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now I'm responsible for your alarm too.

beats.speaker: B

beats.text: I'm family. Why am I getting the public version of what happened to the wedding cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone dropped it off the balcony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does the family version include a name?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me where you were.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want my alibi before giving me family gossip? That's the police version.

beats.text: Why is my report on the missing keys censored? I'm on this committee.

beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make an announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.
